label: JZ Mock A · Paper 2 · Question 18
knowledgePattern: Combine cyclic logarithms with their sign restrictions to find a contradiction
solution:
All three logarithms equal positive numbers. Since logab>0, the numbers a and b lie on the same side of 1: both exceed 1 or both lie between 0 and 1. The other equations force all three a, b and c onto the same side.

Using change of base, the product logablogbclogca equals 1, since the three nonzero fixed-base logarithms cancel cyclically. The right sides multiply to abc, so abc=1.

If all three exceed 1, their product exceeds 1. If all three lie between 0 and 1, their product is less than 1. Both cases contradict abc=1. There are no solutions. Answer D.

hints.title: Use the sign of each logarithm
hints.body: A positive logarithm constrains its argument relative to 1 according to whether the base is above or below 1. Apply that to all three equations.
hints.recap: For a valid base above one, logarithms increase; for a base between zero and one, they decrease.
hints.pitfall: Positive bases need not be greater than one.
hints.pause: Determine which combinations of sides of 1 remain possible.

recall.reminder: For a valid base above one, logarithms increase; for a base between zero and one, they decrease.

hints.title: Combine the cyclic equations
hints.body: Write each logarithm with the same fixed base and multiply the three equations. Retain the restrictions that justify any cancellation.
hints.recap: Change of base expresses a logarithm as a ratio of fixed-base logarithms; the denominator is nonzero for a valid base.
hints.pitfall: A necessary algebraic relation still has to be compatible with the original domains.
hints.pause: Simplify the product relation and compare it with the possible sign cases.
